S1.why: The bracket already points at the tiles, so the number and "percuma" (free of charge) are enough; no noun needed.

S2.why: An invitation to carry on, in the plain verb; no limit word ("had") and no sales line.

S3.s: Kesemua %lld cutling percuma sudah anda gunakan. Semuanya kekal percuma dan terus berfungsi.
S3.back: All 5 cutling free already you used. All-of-them remain free and continue functioning.
S3.why: "sudah anda gunakan" is the native object-first passive, warmer than "telah digunakan" and keeps the person in it; "cutling" from the vocabulary, lowercase in a sentence as the vocabulary writes it; 89 characters with the 5 filled in.

S4.why: The way Malaysian apps word a free allowance; avoids an "Anda boleh…" sentence; 41 characters.

S5.why: "daripada" is the Malaysian word for "out of" ("dari" reads Indonesian); Malay keeps used-then-total order, so plain %lld works without positions.

S6.why: Bold row line kept to the number; "Ruang untuk %@ cutling" read better but runs 25 against the 24 budget; Malay has no plural, so "cutling" fits any number.

S7.s: Simpan sebanyak %@ cutling teks dan %lld imej.
S7.back: Save as-many-as 5,000 cutling text and 500 image.
S7.why: "cutling teks" and "imej" are the vocabulary's own names for the two kinds; "sebanyak" gives the ceiling without repeating "hingga" from the bold line.

S8.why: Malay lists three things with no comma before "dan".

S9.s: Satu pembelian, semua peranti yang log masuk ke Apple Account anda.
S9.back: One purchase, all devices that log in to Apple Account your.
S9.why: Reuses the vocabulary's phrase "peranti yang log masuk ke Apple Account anda" so the account is named the same way everywhere; 67 characters.

S10.why: The everyday Malaysian wording for a one-off payment; "sahaja" carries "nothing recurring".

S11.s: Tiada langganan, iklan atau pendaftaran akaun.
S11.back: No subscription, advertising or registration account.
S11.why: One "tiada" governs the list and "atau" joins a negated list in Malay; repeating "tiada" three times reads like a slogan.

S12.why: The wording Malay App Store apps use for this action, kept in its title case because people know it as a fixed label.

S13.why: The meN- verb form of "pulihkan" for a process in progress, with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: "Buka kunci" is iOS Malay for unlock; "sekali bayar" is how Malaysians say one-off payment in conversation; 25 characters before the price.

S15.why: The same action as S14 with nothing hanging off it while the price loads.

S16.why: Putting it off, not saying no; softer than the system's "Bukan sekarang" (not now).

S17.why: The plain verb iOS Malay uses on close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and a little proud, and "semuanya" takes in the whole grid of room that just opened; 19 characters.

S19.s: Terima kasih kerana menyokong Cutling dan satu-satunya orang yang membinanya.
S19.back: Thank you because supporting Cutling and the-one-and-only person who builds-it.
S19.why: "satu-satunya orang" says plainly that one person makes the app; buying is the support, so the sentence does not name the purchase twice.

S20.s: Selamat kembali. Pembelian anda yang lalu telah dipulihkan.
S20.back: Welcome back. Purchase your that past has been restored.
S20.why: "Selamat kembali" is the usual welcome back; "dipulihkan" matches the "Pulihkan Pembelian" link they just tapped.

S21.why: Same words as the S5 subtitle so sight and VoiceOver agree; no period, as VoiceOver labels go.

S22.s: Anda ada %lld cutling, dengan ruang untuk %@.
S22.back: You have 5 cutling, with room for 5,000.
S22.why: Malay nouns do not change for number, so "%lld cutling" reads right for 1, 2, 5 and 21; "ada" is the spoken have.

S23.s: Cutling sudah dibuka kunci. Ada ruang untuk %@ cutling.
S23.back: Cutling already unlocked. There-is room for 5,000 cutling.
S23.why: "dibuka kunci" is the iOS Malay passive for unlocked; two short spoken sentences.

S24.why: Says it did not finish rather than failed ("gagal"), so there is no blame.

S25.s: App Store tidak dapat dihubungi buat masa ini. Cuba lagi sebentar nanti.
S25.back: App Store cannot be-contacted for time this. Try again a-moment later.
S25.why: "buat masa ini" and "cuba lagi sebentar nanti" are the standard Malaysian phrasing for a temporary outage; 72 characters.

S26.s: App Store tidak mengesahkan pembelian ini.
S26.back: App Store not confirm purchase this.
S26.why: "mengesahkan" is the Malaysian verb for confirm; states the fact and nothing it cannot know.

S27.s: Tiada pembelian Cutling ditemui untuk Apple Account di peranti ini.
S27.back: No purchase Cutling found for Apple Account on device this.
S27.why: "ditemui" (found) is how restore results read in Malay; the vocabulary's longer "yang log masuk" form would run to 83 against the 80 budget.

S28.s: Versi percuma menyimpan %lld cutling. Buka kunci Cutling sekali dan simpan sebanyak mana anda mahu.
S28.back: Version free stores 5 cutling. Open lock Cutling once and save as-many which you want.
S28.why: "sebanyak mana anda mahu" is the Malaysian spoken form of as many as you like, so it sounds right read aloud by Siri; 96 characters.

S29.why: "4 daripada 5 percuma" is 20 against an 18 budget; the slash pair reads at a glance under the list title.

K1.s: %lld percuma habis. Buka kunci di Cutling
K1.back: 5 free used-up. Open lock in Cutling
K1.why: "habis" (used up) is what a Malaysian would say of a free allowance; the capsule is the thing tapped, so "di Cutling" tells where it goes; exactly 38 characters, which "Ketik untuk buka kunci" could not fit.

M1.why: Verb-led like Mac window names; sentence case to match the app's own menu items ("Cutling teks").

M2.why: The same command as M1, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: The vocabulary's word for items with "percuma" after it, as Malay puts the adjective after the noun.

M4.why: The compact pair; "3 daripada 5" is 12 against a 10 budget.

M5.why: The iOS and macOS Malay status word for unlocked; the section already says Cutling.

M6.s: Satu pembelian membuka kunci Cutling pada iPhone, iPad dan Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Active verb with the purchase as subject, which is natural Malay; the list matches S8.

M7.s: Dibuka kunci pada iPhone, iPad dan Mac dengan Apple Account ini.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with Apple Account this.
M7.why: Same status word as M5; "Apple Account ini" points at the account in use on this Mac.

M8.s: Terima kasih kerana membeli Cutling sebelum ia percuma. Ia kekal dibuka kunci.
M8.back: Thank you because buying Cutling before it free. It remains unlocked.
M8.why: Thanks come first because that is how a Malaysian writer would open; "kekal" (remains) tells them nothing changes; 78 characters.
